text: 🤖 Qwen3.8-27B squeezed to 3-bit, 10 GB, and it still matches BF16 on agentic benchmarks Nari Labs' NariQ scores 41.0 on DeepSWE (BF16: 39.8) and 63.8 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (BF16: 62.6). The 2-bit version falls off a cliff, down to 28.6 on DeepSWE. All numbers are self-reported. You need their llama.cpp fork, and an M3 Pro manages about 3.8 tok/s. A 1,000-token reply takes around four minutes.

🧠 Qwen 32B seems to know when a concept was slipped into its context, but it won't say so out loud A new arXiv paper finds the detection signal in the residual stream, then watches it fade in the final layers. Prompting the model with accurate info on how AI introspection works lifts sensitivity from 0.3% to 39.9%, with only 0.6% more false positives. The authors never test whether the model can tell hidden-state edits from plain input manipulation. It may just be spotting a contradiction in the prompt. Code is out for small Qwen models, so anyone can rerun it.

🤖 Anthropic's new Claude Ship lets an AI agent approve code changes on its own Anthropic launched a beta suite for what happens after the PR. Code Review is already live. PR Steward fixes things like failing CI checks, and Claude Approvals signs off on routine changes under policies your team sets. Anthropic says Claude writes most of the Claude Code team's own code, so it wanted everything after the PR to move just as fast.

🤖 Anthropic says Claude settled VP vs. VNP, the arithmetic cousin of P vs. NP Anthropic's formal-math repo has a paper claiming Claude solved it. VP vs. VNP asks the same question as P vs. NP, but for algebraic circuits computing polynomials instead of Boolean problems. It doesn't touch P vs. NP itself, and nobody outside Anthropic has checked the proof yet.

🚨 US moves to blacklist Singapore's Megaspeed over suspected Nvidia chip diversion to China Commerce says it plans to add the data center developer to the Entity List, after investigating it for almost two years, well before the Alice Huang affair story broke. The suspicion is that it helped get restricted Nvidia chips to Chinese companies, and Alibaba is its largest customer. No effective date yet.

🚨 Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok's sexualized deepfakes, minors included Both attorneys general say SpaceX and X Corp. lied about safety and kept safeguards weak on purpose to pull in users for a "lagging product." Virginia's complaint calls it a "market opportunity for more profits." The suits are in state courts, in Richmond and Multnomah County. Baltimore and a group of Tennessee teens have already filed similar cases.

🚨 Google says it just saw the first fully autonomous cyberattack Google's threat team reports criminals have moved past supervised chatbots to software that finds flaws and launches exploits on its own. An exposed server revealed tooling built to automate vulnerability research and exploitation end to end.

🚨 Amazon pays $7.5B for Decart's chip-optimization tech after Anthropic and Nvidia both walked Amazon signed for the Optimization Stack behind the Israeli startup, plus its three co-founders and research team. • Decart already tuned Amazon's Trainium chips in 2025 • Anthropic pulled out of a ~$6B deal in early September • Nvidia refused to reopen talks • Founders stay five years, with a big chunk of the payout in year five

🚨 Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO 10 days after he resigned, and the stock jumps 27% The board voted unanimously after reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman allegedly in contact with a Chinese intelligence officer. It says "senior levels of the United States government" told it his return poses no national security risk, after weeks of insisting reinstatement wasn't on the table.

🤖 HAProxy's lead got Mythos bug reports on his own code, and they were close to unusable Willy Tarreau says two batches of 30 to 50 findings arrived with no reproducers, no patches, no commit ID, and walls of text in single-line paragraphs. A colleague who validated and patched the bugs by hand got far better results. He's a Linux kernel security team member, and he still can't get Mythos access himself.

🤖 A 32GB RTX 5090 now runs a 27B Qwen as your own private ChatGPT, no terminal required GPUPartner's guide installs Unsloth Desktop, loads Qwen3.8-27B at 4-bit with a 128K context, and turns on LAN access, about 10-15 minutes plus downloads. Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini (26.4B, Apache 2.0) is a near-identical 17.6GB fit. The card that makes it comfortable still costs more than a year of most subscriptions.

🚨 Z.ai just dropped GLM 5.4, and so far it's a tweet and nothing else Zhipu's announcement is a bare post with the version number. • No model card or benchmarks yet • No word on pricing or API docs • Open weights and license unconfirmed • No comparison to DeepSeek, Qwen or Kimi

🚨 A 16-year-old YC founder is building AI-guided missiles and pitching "cost per kill" Henrijs Dandzbergs dropped out of high school to start Polemos Industries, which Wired profiles . He's in YC's fall 2026 batch, probably its youngest solo founder ever. The pitch is a cheap, easy-to-build precision missile with jam resistance that fires from portable launchers.

🚨 Bell Canada says an "agentic" attacker got into its systems and took enterprise customer data Bell confirmed the Nov 17 breach, which hit a pre-production Maximo system used to order and provision circuits. Names, job titles, work emails, phone numbers, ticket titles and some network IP addresses may be gone. Bell hasn't named the actor, hasn't said how many customers were hit, and hasn't published the IOCs it's sharing privately.

⚡️ Raschka says pre-training isn't plateauing, and OpenAI's own data backs him up In a new essay , he points to a chart from OpenAI where log-perplexity keeps falling as pre-training scales. It's a next-token metric, not a task score, but it still tracks real-world performance, and he wants the same plot with training FLOPs on the x-axis.

🚨 TSMC just bought $500M of Anthropic at the IPO price TSMC Partners picked up 6,024,096 shares at $83 each, which works out to about 0.03% of a company priced at roughly $1.5T. It's the first half of a board-approved plan to put up to $500M each into Anthropic common stock and OpenAI preferred shares.

🚨 California's Nvidia probe reportedly covers possible criminal law violations Bloomberg reports that the state's investigation reaches past civil territory. That's a different tier of risk for the company that supplies most of the AI chips on earth. Details are thin so far, and an investigation isn't a charge. State prosecutors don't need Washington's permission to make a very bad quarter.

🚨 Anthropic's IPO ran so tight that bankers are complaining Reuters reports Anthropic capped some of its 22 underwriters at four bankers per deal team. Some senior bankers also signed six-month non-competes covering rivals like OpenAI and Cursor. Banks still collected over $500M in fees. The stock jumped 17% on day one, then closed down 8.5% on Friday.

🚨 Trump threatens "tremendous penalties" for US tech firms that build datacenters abroad He said it at a Friday press conference, and he gave no details . He also admitted he hasn't told his own officials. His reasoning is that China "will take all of them," and he told US communities to make developers pay them but not shut the datacenters off.

⚡️ RightNow AI makes Inkling 2 Small's FP4 expert GEMMs 5.1x to 7.5x faster on B300, with identical bits The YC-backed lab tuned kernels for Thinking Machines' 594B MoE on 8 GPUs, running NVFP4 natively. Logits matched on all 599 rows, whether prompts were fed 64 positions per step or 1. They sharded the NVFP4 experts anyway, which SGLang's recipe says can't be done. Each GPU exchanges only the row maximum, and the kernels are open source.

🚨 Together AI's leaked prompts came from a credential its own coding agent committed Together disclosed that an AI coding agent working on its public xorl repo committed a key to a private Hugging Face repo of prompt samples. Someone grabbed it, downloaded samples from MiniMax M3, GLM-5.2 and Kimi K2.6 requests, and went hunting for credentials. Together reverted the commit after its scanner flagged the key. It's still working out which customers were hit, and five of the credentials the thief tested were canaries.

🚨 OpenRouter cuts 3 inference providers and pulls 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention After the MiniMax prompt leak, OpenRouter off-boarded three providers. It also dropped some endpoints as a precaution, beyond the ones researchers flagged. Those endpoints only get ZDR back with assurances and validation, and OpenRouter is adapting the researchers' testing to run these checks continuously.

🚨 Cursor may drop Kimi K2.5 after a House report on Chinese models According to the report , Cursor is exploring a phase-out of PRC base models. • 50-page joint report from Homeland Security and the China Select Committee • Probe started in April 2026 • It named weights from Alibaba, Moonshot, DeepSeek and MiniMax • Cursor is now owned by SpaceX

🤖 Stripe's new evals: coding agents score 78.1% on Stripe integrations, but only 29.4% on strict pass Stripe ran 69 scenarios on 14 model and harness pairs. Agents lean on older APIs from their training data, and they ship code that's almost right. Opus 5.5 checks that a payment succeeded but not whether the order was refunded, so it can ship refunded or disputed orders. The Stripe plugin lifted every agent by 3 to 8 points and cut web searches 96%. Almost correct is how money gets lost.

🚨 Prefill attacks break every major open-weight model FAR.AI tested FAR.AI ran 20+ prefill strategies across multiple model families. You write the first few tokens of the reply yourself, and the model just keeps going. Big reasoning models held up better against generic prefills. Tailored, model-specific ones still got through.

🚨 The Riemann Hypothesis now has a Lean proof, and the Lean and Mathlib communities say it checks out Levent Alpöge's 17M-line library depends only on Mathlib . Dozens of people reproduced the build, a comparator confirmed it proves Mathlib's own RiemannHypothesis statement, and several independent checkers in different languages passed the exported proof, including Lean's kernel.

🚨 Anthropic's IPO bank just gave up its safety net for the stock Morgan Stanley exercised its full 147M-share greenshoe at the $83 IPO price. That lifts total proceeds to about $93.5B, but it also means the bank can't buy shares on the open market if the price slips below $83. A Berenberg analyst notes the bookrunners dropped the option after one day of trading, just as the stock was drifting toward the IPO price.

🚨 House committees say cheap Chinese open-weight models are a US dependency problem The China Select Committee and Homeland Security released a report after probing Anysphere and Airbnb over their use of PRC models. DoorDash got a letter in July. It's a report, not a rule. But if US labs charge premium prices and Qwen and DeepSeek are free, the "restrict them" argument writes itself.
